briefing.summary: Follow the largest submarine canyon on the US West Coast from its head just offshore of Moss Landing onto the steep shelf break nearby. From there, continue further down-canyon if you can: a canyon wall, the traced axis at about 1,000 m and 2,000 m, and the MARS seafloor observatory node are all optional deeper objectives.
facts: Monterey Canyon begins right off the beach at Moss Landing -- so close to shore that MBARI, headquartered there, calls it their 'backyard'.
The main channel runs about 153 km out to sea, with walls up to 1.6-1.7 km high; its published maximum depth, about 3,600 m, lies beyond this tile's western edge.
Just past the head, the seafloor drops from under 50 m to more than 250 m in under 3 km, where the canyon cuts across the continental shelf break.

Turbidity currents -- fast underwater avalanches of sediment -- have been measured moving down this canyon at up to about 7 m/s, some travelling more than 50 km. They happen several times a year in the upper canyon.
The MBARI-operated MARS observatory node, at 891 m, is a real cabled power-and-data outlet for deep-sea science instruments, connected to shore by a 52 km cable.
hazards: Turbidity currents: sudden, fast-moving sediment flows can occur without warning, especially in the upper canyon.
Strong currents generally, including upwelling-driven flow near the canyon rim.
Fishing gear may be present, especially in shallower water near the head.
Total darkness below a few hundred metres.

objectives.title: Locate and scan the canyon head
objectives.hint: The canyon head starts just offshore from Moss Landing, on shallow seabed around 45 m.

objectives.title: Follow the channel onto the shelf break
objectives.hint: Follow the canyon channel west from the head across the shelf break, descending to around 265 m.

objectives.title: Survey a canyon wall (optional, further down-canyon)
objectives.hint: The north canyon wall is far west and down-canyon from the head, around 750 m at its marker.

objectives.title: Reach the canyon axis at about 1,000 m (optional)
objectives.hint: The canyon axis lies just south of the north-wall marker, around 1,000 m deep.

objectives.title: Continue down-canyon to about 2,000 m (optional)
objectives.hint: Continue southwest down the canyon axis to mapped seabed around 2,000 m.

objectives.title: Find the MARS observatory node (optional, long transit)
objectives.hint: The illustrative MARS observatory-node marker lies far west of the head, near 890 m; this tile does not survey the equipment.
